# Database schema

Binding. See [README.md](README.md).

The schema is defined by `panel/src/main/resources/wisper/migrations/V{n}__*.sql`, one
file per change, currently V1 to V33. This document is the map: what each table is for,
who is allowed to write which column, and the invariants a package must not break. Where
this file and a migration disagree, the migration is the truth and this file is a bug.

An applied migration is immutable (`SchemaMigrations` checksums it). Fix forward with a
new file.

---

## 1. Conventions every table follows

### Identity is a UUID generated by the panel

Every primary key is `uuid`, and it is generated in Java with `UUID.randomUUID()` before
the insert. The database has no `DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` and no sequence: an id that
only exists after a round trip cannot be put in a log line, an audit record or a
child row that is being built in the same transaction.

### `version` is what makes an assigned id insertable

Spring Data JDBC decides insert-versus-update from the aggregate. With an
application-assigned id, a non-null id would look like an update of a row that does not
exist. So **every table has `version bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, and every aggregate
record declares it**:

```java
record Service(@Id UUID id, UUID projectId, String name, ServiceKind kind,
               @CreatedDate Instant createdAt, @LastModifiedDate Instant updatedAt,
               @Version Long version) { }
```

A null `version` means new; anything else is an update, and the update is checked
optimistically. There are no exceptions to this, including on append-only tables - a rule
with one exception is a rule somebody applies to the wrong table.

> This is the one place this contract overrides
> [`panel-configuration.md`](panel-configuration.md), which says `@Id Long id`. The rest
> of that file - repositories, `@Query`, table naming, timestamps, ids not object graphs,
> longs in the smallest unit - applies unchanged. Path variables are therefore `UUID`,
> not `long`.

### Timestamps

`timestamptz` everywhere; there is not one naive timestamp in the schema. `created_at` and
`updated_at` come from Java via `@CreatedDate` / `@LastModifiedDate`, because Spring Data
JDBC writes every mapped column on insert and would otherwise overwrite a `DEFAULT now()`
with NULL. The `DEFAULT now()` in the DDL is there for rows a migration inserts.

### Enums are text with a CHECK

No PostgreSQL enum types. Adding a value is then an `ALTER ... DROP CONSTRAINT` plus
`ADD CONSTRAINT` in a new migration, which is cheap and reversible, instead of an
`ALTER TYPE` that cannot run in a transaction with other statements. Every constraint is
named, so a violation says which rule was broken.

Values are `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` and map to a Java enum of the same name.

### Types you will not find, and why

| Not used | Instead | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `jsonb` | `text` holding a JSON document | PgJDBC sends a `String` parameter as varchar and PostgreSQL will not implicitly cast that to `jsonb`. A `jsonb` column forces a `PGobject` converter into every package that writes one. Nothing in the panel queries inside these documents. |
| `inet` | `text` holding an IPv4/IPv6 literal | Same cast problem. |
| `numeric` / `double` | `bigint` in the smallest unit | Bytes, millicores, counts. |
| PostgreSQL enums | `text` + CHECK | See above. |

`text[]` **is** used, in the seven places where the value is genuinely a list the database
has to search or the node has to receive as a vector: `node.tags`,
`service.required_tags`, `service.command`, `service.entrypoint`, `cron_task.command`,
`certificate.subject_alternative_names`, `api_token.scopes`. Spring Data JDBC maps these
to `String[]` with no converter.

### Encryption at rest

Any column that holds a value the panel must be able to read back is stored in one
envelope format:

```
v<keyVersion>.<base64url nonce>.<base64url ciphertext>      AES-GCM
```

One text column, so rotating a key rewrites one value and a reader always knows which key
produced what it is holding. A CHECK constraint on each such column rejects anything that
is not shaped like an envelope, which catches the mistake that matters - a plaintext value
written into an encrypted column.

**Encrypted** (reversible, because the panel has to use the value):

| Column | Used for |
|---|---|
| `account.totp_secret` | verifying TOTP codes |
| `service.webhook_secret` | HMAC of an incoming Git webhook |
| `service.repository_credential` | cloning a private repository |
| `secret.value` | environment values sent to the node |
| `database_engine.admin_password` | creating customer databases |
| `managed_database.db_password` | showing the connection string, rotating |
| `backup_destination.secret_access_key` | pushing to S3 |
| `backup_destination.archive_passphrase` | encrypting the archive before it leaves the node |

**Hashed** (SHA-256, or BCrypt where noted) - the panel only ever compares, so it must not
be able to read these back:

`account.password_hash` (BCrypt), `account_recovery_code.code_hash`,
`session.session_id_hash`, `node.credential_hash`, `node_enrollment_token.token_hash`,
`api_token.token_hash`.

**Never stored at all**: TLS private keys. The node owns the certificate and the key never
leaves it (design §11.3). `certificate` holds metadata only.

### Names that differ from the design doc's §6 sketch

| Sketch | Actual | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `users` | `account` | `user` is reserved in PostgreSQL and Spring Data JDBC quotes nothing for you. |
| `database` | `managed_database` | `DATABASE` is a keyword. The Java package is still `database`; the record is `ManagedDatabase`. |
| `scheduled_task` | `cron_task` | `scheduled_tasks` is db-scheduler's table (V1). Two tables one letter apart, one holding customer intent and one internal jobs, is a query written against the wrong one. |
| `stat_sample` rollups | one `stat_rollup` with `granularity` | Two identical tables differing only in bucket width would be the same record and the same use-case twice. |

Tables the sketch does not name, added because the feature does not work without them:
`account_recovery_code`, `quota_override`, `deployment_log`, `database_engine`,
`restore_run`.

## 2. The ownership rule

> **The panel owns intent. The node owns fact. No column is written from both
> directions.** (AGENTS.md §4.2, design §5.1)

This is the rule the predecessor broke, and it is the one that is easiest to break by
accident, because intent and fact often live on the same row. Where they do, the column
list is split and the halves are labelled in the migration. The table below is the
authoritative list.

| Table | Panel writes (intent) | Node writes (fact) |
|---|---|---|
| `node` | everything | nothing |
| `node_status` | nothing | everything |
| `service` | everything | nothing |
| `placement` | `state`, `pinned`, `reason`, `placed_at`, `released_at` | `reported_state`, `reported_at`, `container_id`, `running_image_digest`, `restart_count`, `last_exit_code`, `last_error`, `health` |
| `volume` | `name`, `mount_path`, `size_bytes`, `read_only`, `backup_enabled` | `used_bytes`, `used_bytes_measured_at`, `inode_count`, `host_path`, `reported_state`, `last_error` |
| `managed_database` | everything except the two below | `used_bytes`, `used_bytes_measured_at` |
| `database_engine` | everything except the four below | `reported_state`, `reported_at`, `disk_bytes_used`, `last_error` |
| `cron_task` | `schedule`, `command`, `enabled`, `timeout_seconds`, `concurrency_policy`, `next_run_at` | `last_run_at`, `last_finished_at`, `last_exit_code`, `last_duration_ms`, `last_error` |
| `certificate` | nothing | everything |
| `deployment` | everything except `release_path`, `image_digest` | `release_path`, `image_digest` |
| `restore_point` | the request | `object_key`, `size_bytes`, `checksum_sha256`, `finished_at`, `state` |
| `stat_sample`, `stat_rollup` | nothing (rollup is computed panel-side from node data) | everything |

"Node writes" means: the gRPC handlers in `lhqm.furimeo.wisper.grpc` write it from a
report. No controller, no use-case and no admin screen may touch one of those columns.

### Generation semantics

`node.desired_generation` is a monotonically increasing counter owned by the panel. It is
bumped whenever anything in that node's spec changes, and never decreased or reset.
`node_status.applied_generation` is what the node says it has converged to, and starts at
`-1` for "never reported".

- `applied = desired` - converged.
- `applied < desired` - in flight, or the node is behind.
- `applied > desired` - impossible; it means two panels are pointed at one node.

On reconnect the panel sends the **full** spec, never a delta (design §5.2), so a node
that was away for a week needs no catch-up logic.

## 3. Table map

### Identity and access

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `account` | A person who can sign in. | `email` is stored lower-cased and is unique; a CHECK enforces the lower-casing so no functional index is needed. `platform_role` ∈ `ADMIN`, `CUSTOMER`; `ADMIN` is `ROLE_ADMIN` and gates `/admin/**`. `totp_confirmed_at` cannot be set without `totp_secret`, so a half-finished 2FA enrolment never locks anyone out. |
| `account_recovery_code` | Single-use TOTP recovery codes. | Hashed. `used_at` set on consumption; rows are not deleted, so "you have used 3 of 8" is answerable. |
| `session` | One row per signed-in browser. | **Not** Spring Session JDBC - that dependency is not on the classpath and the servlet container still holds the `HttpSession`. This table is what makes an active-session list, "sign out everywhere" and a sign-in location history possible. Only the `auth` package writes it. `second_factor_at` is null while the TOTP challenge is outstanding; such a session may reach `/login/**` and nothing else. |
| `api_token` | Scoped bearer tokens for `/api/v1/**`. | `token_hash` unique; `token_prefix` is in the clear so a leaked token in a log can be matched to a row. `scopes` is non-empty and constrained by `<@` against the known set, so a token cannot request a permission nothing checks. A null `organization_id` means the token acts across every organization the account belongs to. |

### Tenancy and limits

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `plan` | A named bundle of limits. | At most one row with `is_default`, enforced by a partial unique index. No price column: billing is out of scope. Archived plans keep working for who is on them; `organization.plan_id` is `RESTRICT`, so a plan in use cannot be deleted. |
| `quota` | `(plan, resource) -> limit`. | **A resource with no row on the plan is limited to zero.** `EnforceQuota` must never read a missing row as unlimited; that turns forgetting to seed a plan into an unmetered platform. |
| `quota_override` | A per-organization exception. | `reason` is required and non-blank. Resolution order: an unexpired override, then the plan's `quota`, then zero. |
| `organization` | The tenant. | `status = 'SUSPENDED'` and `suspended_at IS NOT NULL` are the same fact, enforced by a CHECK. Suspension blocks writes; it does not stop a customer's containers. |
| `member` | Membership and role. | Unique per `(organization, account)`. `accepted_at` null means an invitation is outstanding and grants nothing. Roles: `OWNER`, `ADMIN`, `DEVELOPER`, `VIEWER`. |
| `project` | A grouping inside an organization. | `slug` unique per organization. |

**The authorization join is the only source of ownership**:

```
account -> member -> organization -> project -> service -> (everything else)
```

There is deliberately no denormalised `organization_id` on `service` or its children. Two
places to read ownership from is one place to get it wrong.

### Workloads

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `service` | The deployable unit. `kind` ∈ `APP`, `SITE`. | An `APP` must have an `image`; a `SITE` must have a `build_preset` and a `build_output_dir` and must **not** have an image or a container port, because a static site is files on disk with no process (design §5.5). `runtime_isolation = 'RUNC'` requires a non-blank `isolation_reason`, which the panel displays as a warning (design §11.6). `desired_state` is customer intent and is never written from a status report, so "stopped by the customer" and "crashed" stay different facts. `command` and `entrypoint` are argv arrays, never shell strings. |
| `placement` | Which node runs a service, plus what that node reports. | **At most one `ACTIVE` placement per service** (partial unique index). It is partial so a `DRAINING` placement and its replacement can coexist during a migration. `node_id` is `ON DELETE RESTRICT`: drain a node before deleting it. `pinned` is set once a volume exists; a pinned placement is never moved by the scheduler (design §7.8). |
| `env_var` | Plain environment variables. | Name matches `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` and may not start with `WISPER_`, which the platform injects. Unique per service. Readable in the UI. |
| `secret` | Environment values that must not be readable. | Same name rules. Encrypted envelope, enforced by CHECK. **The API never returns `value`.** A separate table rather than an `is_secret` flag, because the difference changes how it is stored, whether a GET returns it and what an audit entry may contain - three runtime `if`s somebody eventually forgets. |
| `volume` | Persistent storage. | On the node: `/var/lib/wisper/volumes/<service-id>/<volume-id>` - ids, not slugs, so renaming a service never moves a directory. This layout is fixed; changing it means moving customer data (design §11.1). `mount_path` must be absolute, must not contain `..`, and may not be a system directory. `size_bytes` is the XFS project quota the node applies; where `node_status.quota_enforceable` is false the limit is advisory. |
| `cron_task` | Customer cron inside a service. | `command` is argv and non-empty. The schedule is evaluated **on the node**, not by db-scheduler: a cron that must fire while the panel is unreachable cannot have the panel in its path. `next_run_at` is a panel-side display value the node does not read. |

### Deployment

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `deployment` | One attempt to publish a version. | `sequence` is the per-service number the customer sees, allocated as `max(sequence) + 1` inside the inserting transaction; the unique index on `(service_id, sequence)` is what makes two concurrent deploys resolve rather than collide silently. **At most one `is_current` per service** (partial unique index), and a current deployment must have `status = 'SUCCEEDED'`. Rollback is a new row pointing at the one being undone via `rolled_back_from_deployment_id`, so the history reads forwards. `node_id` is `SET NULL`: retiring a node must not take the history with it. |
| `deployment_log` | Build output, one line per row. | `(deployment_id, sequence)` unique - this is both the ordering and the SSE resume cursor, and it rejects a duplicated line when a node redelivers a chunk after a reconnect. Rows rather than one growing text column, because rewriting a whole column per line is how the predecessor's build log became its slowest write. |

### Edge

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | A hostname pointed at a service. | **`hostname` is globally unique**, not per organization: two customers cannot both claim `example.com`, and the node's on-demand-TLS `ask` handler answers from a table keyed by hostname alone. Stored lower-cased as an IDNA A-label, enforced by CHECK. At most one `PRIMARY` domain per service. `kind = 'WILDCARD'` and a `*.` prefix are the same fact, enforced by CHECK. In v1 a hostname belongs to exactly one node, because the node owns the certificate and certificates are not shared. |
| `certificate` | Panel-side metadata about a TLS certificate. | Entirely node-reported. **No private key column, ever.** At most one row per domain in state `ISSUED`/`RENEWING`; superseded rows stay for the history. An issued certificate must carry `not_before` and `not_after`, so the expiry warning always has something to read. |

### Nodes

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `node` | The record and the operator's intent. | `fingerprint` is unique - that uniqueness **is** the VM-clone detector (design §7.3). A node not in lifecycle `CREATED` must have all three of `fingerprint`, `public_key`, `credential_hash`, or it could not be checked for cloning. `credential_hash` has a unique index because it is read on every gRPC call the node makes: the hottest index in the schema. `desired_generation` is monotonic and never reset. |
| `node_enrollment_token` | The single-use bootstrap token. | Hashed. TTL is `wisper.node.enrollment-token-ttl` (15 minutes). `used_at` must be set in the same transaction that writes `node.credential_hash`, so a replay finds it spent. A token belongs to exactly one node record and can enrol no other. A row cannot be both used and revoked. |
| `node_status` | Everything the node reports. | Primary key **is** the foreign key, so the one-to-one cannot drift into a one-to-many. `runsc_available = false` means the node falls back to `runc` and the panel shows it as less isolated rather than refusing to work (design §7.2). `running_workload_count <= workload_count`, enforced. |

### Managed databases

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `database_engine` | A PostgreSQL or MySQL server on a node. | **One `SHARED` instance per engine per node** (partial unique index); a node may also carry any number of `DEDICATED` ones. `mode = 'DEDICATED'` and a non-null `organization_id` are the same fact, enforced by CHECK. No two engines may bind the same port on one node. Shared by default because a few hundred private database containers at 30-50 MB idle each is a node nobody can afford (design §8.1). |
| `managed_database` | One customer database plus its user. | Name and user are unique **within the engine**, which is where a collision would actually happen. `database_engine_id` is `RESTRICT`: an engine still holding customer databases is not deletable. Exactly one user per database, so there is no grant table; a customer needing two credentials creates two databases. |

### Backup and restore

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `backup_destination` | Where snapshots are pushed. | A null `organization_id` is a platform-wide destination every organization may use; the unique index is `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` so those still cannot share a name. An `S3` row must have endpoint, bucket and credentials; a `LOCAL` row must have an absolute path. `RESTRICT` from both `backup` and `restore_point`: a bucket still holding restorable snapshots is not removable by accident. |
| `backup` | A **policy**: what, how often, where, how long. | Exactly one of `volume_id` / `managed_database_id`, matching `target_kind`. Both are `ON DELETE CASCADE`, not `SET NULL` - a policy for a target that no longer exists has nothing to run, and `SET NULL` would have to satisfy the exactly-one CHECK, which it cannot, so deleting a volume would fail instead. A null `schedule` means the policy runs only when somebody presses the button. Retention is both `retention_count` and `retention_days`, and whichever bites first wins. |
| `restore_point` | An **artefact**: one snapshot that exists. | Built to outlive everything that produced it: `backup_id`, `volume_id`, `managed_database_id` and `node_id` are all `SET NULL`, and `target_label` carries a human-readable copy of what was backed up, because the moment a customer needs a restore is usually the moment after something was deleted. Deliberately has no exactly-one-target CHECK, for the `SET NULL` reason above. A row in state `AVAILABLE` must have `object_key`, `size_bytes` and `finished_at`, or nothing could restore from it. |
| `restore_run` | One attempt to restore. | Exists because "a backup you have not restored is not a backup" (design §8.3): restoring is a button, and an asynchronous button needs somewhere to report progress or the screen behind it is a blank frame. `mode = 'VERIFY'` restores into a scratch area and throws it away, which is how a snapshot is proven restorable; `IN_PLACE` overwrites and always takes a `PRE_RESTORE` snapshot first, recorded in `safety_restore_point_id`. **At most one in-flight run per target** volume or database, enforced by partial unique indexes: two concurrent restores into one target interleave their writes and produce something that was never a valid snapshot of anything. |

### Observability

| Table | What it holds | Invariants |
|---|---|---|
| `stat_sample` | Raw samples pushed over `PushStats`. | A null `service_id` is a node-level sample. `(node_id, service_id, sampled_at)` is unique with `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, which is what makes `PushStats` idempotent: a reconnecting node resends what it is unsure landed, and the duplicate is rejected instead of doubling a chart. `sampled_at` is when the node measured, not when the panel stored - a chart drawn on arrival time shows spikes that never happened. Retention: 48 hours, then deleted by the `stats` package. |
| `stat_rollup` | Hourly and daily aggregates. | `bucket_start` must be aligned to `granularity` in UTC, enforced by CHECK. `(granularity, node_id, service_id, bucket_start)` unique with `NULLS NOT DISTINCT`, so re-running the rollup over a window corrects rather than duplicates. `sample_count` is the weight for any further aggregation and the way to tell a quiet hour from a missing one. Retention: `HOUR` 30 days, `DAY` 400 days. |
| `audit_log` | Every state-changing action. | Append-only. Actor references are `SET NULL` so the trail outlives the actor, and the identity survives in `actor_label`, which is required and non-blank. The CHECK is phrased as "these ids must be null for this actor_kind" rather than "that one must be set" - `SET NULL` is an `UPDATE` that has to satisfy the constraint, so demanding presence would make deleting an account fail outright. `DENIED` outcomes are recorded too: "somebody tried and was refused" is the entry an incident is reconstructed from. `action` is a dotted stable value (`service.start`), not prose, because it is filtered on. `detail` never contains a secret value. |

### Framework

`scheduled_tasks` (V1) is db-scheduler's, reproduced exactly as
[`panel-configuration.md`](panel-configuration.md) specifies. It is not ours to change.
`schema_version` is created by `SchemaMigrations` itself and has no migration.

---

## 4. Access paths the indexes exist for

Every index in this schema was added for a query somebody will write. If you need a path
that is not here, add the index in a new migration and add the row.

| Query | Index |
|---|---|
| Authenticate a node on every RPC | `node_credential_hash_key` |
| Find a node by machine fingerprint (enrol, clone detection) | `node_fingerprint_key` |
| Candidate nodes for placement | `node_placeable_idx`, `node_tags_idx` (GIN) |
| Mark nodes lost after the heartbeat timeout | `node_status_heartbeat_idx` |
| Build a node's spec: everything it must run | `placement_active_by_node_idx` |
| Resolve a hostname to a route | `domain_hostname_key` |
| Certificates expiring soon | `certificate_expiry_idx` |
| Deployments for a service, newest first | `deployment_by_service_recent_idx` |
| What is live for a service | `deployment_current_idx` |
| The deployment worker's queue | `deployment_pending_idx` |
| Stream build logs, resuming after line N | `deployment_log_cursor_key` |
| Node metrics over a window | `stat_sample_node_window_idx`, `stat_rollup_node_window_idx` |
| Service metrics over a window | `stat_sample_service_window_idx`, `stat_rollup_service_window_idx` |
| Authenticate an API token | `api_token_hash_key` |
| Authenticate a session | `session_id_hash_key` |
| Audit log, platform-wide / per tenant / per object / per node | `audit_log_recent_idx`, `audit_log_by_organization_idx`, `audit_log_by_target_idx`, `audit_log_by_node_idx` |
| Backup policies that are due | `backup_due_idx` |
| Snapshots past their retention | `restore_point_expiring_idx` |

---

## 5. Deletion

Deleting is arranged so that metadata cascades and evidence does not.

- **CASCADE** down the tenancy tree: `organization -> project -> service -> {deployment,
  domain, env_var, secret, volume, cron_task, placement}`, and `account -> {session,
  api_token, member, recovery codes}`. Deleting a tenant is an explicit, confirmed,
  destructive act.
- **RESTRICT** where deleting would strand something: `placement -> node` (drain a node
  before deleting it), `managed_database -> database_engine`, `backup -> destination`,
  `restore_point -> destination`, `organization -> plan`.
- **SET NULL** where the row must survive its reference: every actor column on
  `audit_log`, every target column on `restore_point` and `restore_run`,
  `deployment.node_id`, `certificate.node_id`, and the `*_by_account_id` columns.

A row disappearing from this database does **not** delete bytes on a node. The node
removes containers that are no longer in its spec, and it never deletes volume data
except on an explicit purge - "cannot see it" is not "does not exist" (AGENTS.md §4.5).
That is why the confirmations in the UI matter.

---

## 6. Verifying a change

The migrations were checked by applying all 33 to a real PostgreSQL 17, once through
`psql` and once through the exact statement list the panel's own `SqlStatements` splitter
produces, then seeding one row in every table and asserting each partial unique index,
CHECK and referential action fires as intended. Do the same for a new migration; the
splitter drops line comments and understands string literals and `$body$` blocks, so
write SQL normally, but do not put `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` in a migration - every
statement in a file runs in one transaction.
